newsitem.title: UK: BA to call at Pisa on Israel-UK cargo route.
newsitem.headline: BA to call at Pisa on Israel-UK cargo route.

text.p: British Airways Plc has decided to stop over at Pisa, Italy, to pick up traffic on its planned new Israel-UK cargo services, due to start in February, said manager-outsourced capacity of BA World Cargo, Graham Bunsell.
"There are two reasons for the Pisa call on the westbound leg only of the flights, which will initially start on a weekly basis and progressively increase to twice-weekly," he told Reuters.

First, he said, the Airbus Industrie A300B4 converted freighter used for the service on a wet-lease basis from British carrier Channel Express would suffer a cargo payload penalty if it operated direct from Tel Aviv to London Gatwick. Wet-leasing covers the hire of both plane and crew.
Outward capacity is around 38 tonnes, as loads have to be reduced to allow for the carriage of maximum fuel, he added.

But on the return leg "By stopping at Pisa (and refuelling), we will be able to take up 42 to 43 tonnes on each flight. At Pisa, mainly apparel and shoes will be loaded, which will be trucked down from the Florence/Prato region and will be mainly bound for the U.S. market via our onward flights from London," he said.
Bunsell added that because of slot landing restrictions at Gatwick, return cargo flights from Israel would have to land later in the afternoon than originally anticipated.
"This extra time gives us the opportunity to call at Pisa," he noted.

He said BA was confident the new cargo route, which BA has been trying to launch in the face of opposition from the Israeli authorities about the possible use of noisy or unsuitably registered aircraft, would be a success.

"Israel is probably the only place in the Near East that is industrialised enough to support outbound (from the UK) and inbound cargo traffic. Ex-Uk airfreight business to Israel is expanding particularly fast," he said. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +0171 542 7706 Fax +0171 542 5017
